sourceDecisionQuestions.question: The source uses a chalk line (línea de tiza) and describes workers stretching and snapping it. Archived cordeau traceur may not explicitly distinguish chalk from another line-marking system. Confirm French trade and regional sense before scored/audio use.

First course and starter strip are distinct source concepts. Archived premier rang and bande de départ must be checked against the approved roof product and regional terminology; do not collapse the strip into a generic first row.

The foreman marks points on the plan and the overhang measurement is on the job plan. Confirm whether the intended points are physical marks on a drawing or site layout marks made according to it; do not invent a numeric overhang or universal placement dimension.

Source overhang is roof eave projection in this job plan; archived débord may be broader. Confirm the French dictionary sense and the approved plan/product detail before using as an installation command.

Source speaking asks only to show a worker where to run the first-course chalk line. Archived speaking adds the overhang measurement and approved product method. Keep extra process questions separate from this direct learner objective.
